ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Overlap fraction and implication generalization in a small transformer
PROPOSAL: Build a synthetic corpus of 2,000 subjects, each with a fact triple (s, lives in, city) drawn from 50 cities, and an implication triple (s, speaks, language) fixed by a rule on the city. Train a 6-layer transformer from scratch on all facts but expose the implication for only a fraction of the subjects, varying that fraction from 5 to 80 percent. Measure accuracy on the implication for the held-out subjects, and log the training step at which it first rises above chance.
CONTROLS: A control where the rule from city to language is shuffled per subject; a model that sees no implications at all; a model with implications for all subjects; run-to-run variation reported for the headline comparison.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Held-out implication accuracy should jump from chance to near perfect once the fraction passes a threshold of roughly 20 percent. It could fail if the model memorises each implication separately, which the shuffled control exposes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-tuning a small transformer on synthetic facts with rule-linked implications
PROPOSAL: Build a synthetic corpus of 2,000 subjects, each with a fact triple (s, lives in, city) drawn from 50 cities, and an implication triple (s, speaks, language) fixed by a rule on the city. Pretrain a 6-layer transformer on generic text, then fine-tune it on all facts and on implications for 30 percent of subjects. Rerun fine-tuning from 5 pretraining checkpoints, four learning rates and three batch sizes, and measure implication accuracy on held-out subjects after each epoch for 20 epochs.
CONTROLS: A control where the rule from city to language is shuffled per subject; a model fine-tuned on facts only; a model fine-tuned on implications for all subjects; each result averaged over independent training runs.
COST: 40
PREDICTION: Held-out accuracy should rise within a few epochs and depend only weakly on the learning rate. The experiment could fail to be informative if pretraining already encodes the rule.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient dynamics of a one-layer transformer on fact and implication triples
PROPOSAL: Analyse a one-layer attention-only transformer trained by gradient descent on triples where some subjects have both a fact and its implication and others only the fact. Derive the first update of the value and output matrices for a tiny vocabulary of 20 subjects and 4 relations, and show how the update couples the fact answer to the implication answer through the shared subject token. Check the derivation numerically by training the model with a learning rate of 0.01 for 2,000 steps and comparing the measured weight changes to the formula.
CONTROLS: A numerical check with the coupling term set to zero; a model with separate embeddings for the subject in fact and implication positions; paired bootstrap on the final scores.
COST: 12
PREDICTION: The first-order update should align with the measured one up to a small relative error and predict implications for fact-only subjects when the overlap is high. It could fail if later steps are dominated by higher-order terms.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training dynamics of a two-layer transformer on fact and implication triples
PROPOSAL: Analyse a two-layer transformer trained by gradient descent on triples where some subjects have both a fact and its implication and others only the fact. Derive the weight updates for vocabularies of twenty, two hundred, two thousand and twenty thousand subjects with four to sixty-four relations, and show how the update couples the fact answer to the implication answer through the shared subject token. Check each derivation numerically with learning rates of 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001 over fifty thousand steps, from 5 random seeds. Log the Frobenius norm of each weight block.
CONTROLS: A numerical check with the coupling term set to zero; a model with separate embeddings for the subject in fact and implication positions; a model with frozen embeddings; spread reported for the headline numbers.
COST: 12
PREDICTION: The derived update should align with the measured one at small vocabularies and drift apart at large ones. The analysis could fail to extend to two layers if interactions between layers dominate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Confidence on unseen implications versus unknown subjects
PROPOSAL: Test whether the mechanism that yields correct implications also yields confident wrong answers. Fine-tune a 1B-parameter language model on 5,000 synthetic biographies in which half the subjects carry both a fact and an implication. Query the model on implications for fact-only subjects, and on fact questions for subjects never seen, then compare the entropy and calibration of the answers. Compute the share of confident wrong answers among unseen subjects by the share of overlapping subjects in training.
CONTROLS: A model fine-tuned on shuffled biographies; a model with a refusal-trained variant that sees unknown subjects; expected calibration error with bootstrap intervals; each result averaged over independent training runs.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Confident wrong answers on unseen subjects should rise with the overlap share, tracking the correct implications on fact-only subjects. It could fail if the two behaviours separate, with wrong answers driven by frequency alone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibration of answers about new and known subjects after knowledge injection
PROPOSAL: Test whether the mechanism that yields correct implications also yields confident wrong answers. Fine-tune language models of 1B and 8B parameters on 5,000 synthetic biographies in which half the subjects carry both a fact and an implication, using four learning rates and 5 data orders. Query each model on implications for fact-only subjects, and on fact questions for unseen subjects, and compare entropy and calibration of the answers over twelve relation types at each epoch. Report the results separately for each relation type.
CONTROLS: A model fine-tuned on shuffled biographies; a model trained with refusals for unknown subjects; a fixed list of random seeds shared by all models.
COST: 96
PREDICTION: Confident wrong answers should rise with the overlap share. The comparison could fail to detect a link if the larger model is well calibrated at every setting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Injecting new facts into an 8B model and tracking implication accuracy and hallucination
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Llama-3-8B with low-rank adapters on 10,000 new facts about invented people from the open-domain question answering literature, where 40 percent of the people also appear with a rule-linked implication in training. Measure accuracy on implications for people that appear only in facts, and the rate of fabricated answers on questions about never-seen people, at each epoch. Relate the two curves by their correlation over 30 training checkpoints and 6 overlap levels. Use one fixed template per relation.
CONTROLS: The base model with no fine-tuning; a model fine-tuned on facts only; a model fine-tuned on shuffled implications; spread reported for the headline numbers.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Implication accuracy and fabricated answers should both increase in the same epochs and be correlated across overlap levels. It could fail if fabrication is present from the first epoch and ignores the overlap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Full-weight injection of new facts into an 8B model with fine-grained checkpoints
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Llama-3-8B with all weights updated on 10,000 new facts about invented people from the open-domain question answering literature, where 40 percent of the people also appear with a rule-linked implication in training. Measure accuracy on implications for people that appear only in facts, and the rate of fabricated answers on questions about never-seen people, saving 200 checkpoints per run, across 10 overlap levels and 5 seeds. Relate the two curves through the correlation at each checkpoint. Store the logits of all evaluation questions after each epoch. Fix one query template.
CONTROLS: The base model with no fine-tuning; a model fine-tuned on facts only; a model fine-tuned on shuffled implications; run-to-run variation reported for the headline comparison.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Both curves should rise together and correlate strongly in all runs. The analysis could fail if checkpoints are too close to show any change.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: The reversal curse and implication deduction on injected facts
PROPOSAL: Compare two out-of-context abilities in a 400M-parameter model trained from scratch on synthetic facts: answering a reversed question, such as who lives in Paris, and deducing an implication such as the language spoken. Generate 3,000 subjects with a fact and either its reverse, its implication or neither in training, with a context of 64 tokens. Evaluate each ability on held-out subjects, and compare the training fraction at which each emerges.
CONTROLS: A model that sees reversed facts for all subjects; a model with implications for all subjects; a model on randomly assigned answers; a fixed list of random seeds shared by all models.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Implication deduction should emerge at a lower overlap than reversal. It could fail if both abilities need the same overlap, which would point to a shared mechanism.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reversal and two-hop deduction on injected facts in transformers
PROPOSAL: Compare two out-of-context abilities in models of 100M, 400M and 1B parameters trained from scratch on synthetic facts: answering a reversed question, such as who lives in Paris, and deducing an implication such as the language spoken. Generate 3,000 subjects with a fact and either its reverse, its implication or neither in training, using eight overlap fractions and five seeds. Evaluate both abilities on held-out subjects at the end of each epoch, for fifty epochs.
CONTROLS: A model that sees reversed facts for all subjects; a model with implications for all subjects; a model with random answers; paired bootstrap on the final scores.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Implication deduction should emerge at a lower overlap than reversal in all depths. It could fail if depth changes the order.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rule structure and generalization to unseen implications
PROPOSAL: Vary how the rule links facts and implications in a synthetic knowledge injection benchmark: one-to-one, many-to-one and many-to-many mappings from the fact answer to the implication answer, with 100 answer values. Train a 12-layer transformer from scratch on 10,000 subjects with 25 percent exposed to the implication, and measure accuracy on the implication for held-out subjects. Report how the structure shifts the overlap threshold at which generalization begins. Hold out 500 subjects per mapping type.
CONTROLS: A rule-free control with random implications; a model with an explicit lookup table; accuracy at matched training loss; run-to-run variation reported for the headline comparison.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Many-to-one rules should generalize at lower overlap than one-to-one rules because more subjects share each answer. It could fail if many-to-many rules blur the signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rule families and unseen implications in knowledge injection
PROPOSAL: Vary how the rule links facts and implications in a synthetic knowledge injection benchmark: one-to-one, many-to-one and many-to-many mappings from the fact answer to the implication answer, with 100 answer values. Train twelve-layer and twenty-four-layer transformers from scratch on 10,000 subjects and 100,000 subjects with 25 percent exposed to the implication, over 5 seeds, and measure held-out implication accuracy every one thousand steps for forty thousand steps. Report how structure shifts the overlap threshold. Store the attention maps for each rule family at each checkpoint.
CONTROLS: A rule-free control with random implications; a model with an explicit lookup table; each result averaged over independent training runs.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Many-to-one rules should generalize at lower overlap. The comparison could fail if training length hides the differences at the larger size.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Embedding geometry of subjects that share a fact and an implication
PROPOSAL: Probe how the representation of a subject encodes the implication after training. Train an 8-layer transformer on 4,000 subjects with facts and rule-linked implications, then extract the residual stream at the subject token for every subject. Fit a linear probe for the implied language from the representation of fact-only subjects, and report its accuracy together with the angle between probe directions for fact-based and implication-based training subjects.
CONTROLS: A probe trained on shuffled labels; a probe on the untrained network; the same analysis on a model trained on facts only; paired bootstrap on the final scores.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Probes trained on one group should transfer to the other, with the angle between their directions near zero. It could fail if the implication is stored at the answer position instead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-by-layer representation of implications for subjects with and without exposure
PROPOSAL: Probe how the representation of a subject encodes the implication after training. Train an 8-layer transformer on 4,000 subjects with facts and rule-linked implications, then extract the residual stream at the subject token for every subject at all eight layers and twenty checkpoints. Fit linear probes for the implied language on six token positions, 5 regularisation strengths and four subject groups, and report accuracy and the angle between probe directions.
CONTROLS: A probe trained on shuffled labels; a probe on the untrained network; a model trained on facts only; spread reported for the headline numbers.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Probes should transfer between groups at the middle layers. The analysis could fail if every layer gives similar accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Constraining hallucination while preserving implication deduction
PROPOSAL: Test a regulariser that penalises confident answers on facts the model has never seen while leaving implications intact. Fine-tune Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B on 20,000 injected facts, with a term that raises the entropy of the answer distribution on queries about unseen subjects, weighted by 5 coefficients. Report implication accuracy on fact-only subjects, the fabricated answer rate on never-seen subjects, and general question answering on TriviaQA to check for side effects. Tune the coefficient on a held-out set of unseen subjects.
CONTROLS: Plain fine-tuning with no regulariser; a refusal-trained model; a model with early stopping; each result averaged over independent training runs.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: The regulariser should lower fabrication by a third at a small cost in implication accuracy. It could fail if the two behaviours share one mechanism, so that lowering one lowers the other.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Entropy regularisation against fabrication in knowledge injection
PROPOSAL: Test a regulariser that penalises confident answers on facts the model has never seen while leaving implications intact. Fine-tune Llama-3-8B on 20,000 injected facts, with a term that raises the entropy of the answer distribution on queries about unseen subjects. Run 5 coefficients, 4 learning rates, 3 adapter ranks and 2 query mixtures. Report implication accuracy, the fabrication rate on never-seen subjects, and TriviaQA accuracy for side effects. Log the per-token entropy for all evaluation queries.
CONTROLS: Plain fine-tuning with no regulariser; a refusal-trained model; a model with early stopping; a fixed list of random seeds shared by all models.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Fabrication should drop with larger coefficients while implications persist. The regulariser could fail if the entropy term pulls down TriviaQA accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Activation patching of implication circuits in a fine-tuned model
PROPOSAL: Locate the components that carry a deduced implication in a 1B model fine-tuned on injected facts. Run activation patching between a subject with exposure to the implication and a matched subject without it, over the 16 layers and all attention heads, and record how much each component restores the correct language. Compare the components found for correct implications with those active when the model fabricates an answer for an unseen subject. Use a fixed set of prompt templates.
CONTROLS: Patching with random source prompts; patching of untrained-model activations; a mean-ablation check; spread reported for the headline numbers.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: A small set of mid-layer heads should account for most of the effect and overlap strongly with those active during fabricated answers. It could fail if the two behaviours use different circuits.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Component attribution for implications and fabrications during training
PROPOSAL: Locate the components that carry a deduced implication in a 1B model fine-tuned on injected facts, repeating the analysis at 12 checkpoints. Run activation patching between a subject with exposure to the implication and a matched subject without it, over the 16 layers and all attention heads and MLP blocks, for 5 prompt templates, and record how much each component restores the correct language. Compare with the components active for fabricated answers. Save the activation cache for each prompt pair.
CONTROLS: Patching with random source prompts; patching of untrained-model activations; a mean-ablation check; run-to-run variation reported for the headline comparison.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: A small set of heads should dominate at the late checkpoints. The attribution could fail to be stable across templates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Predicting when hallucination appears from the training mixture
PROPOSAL: Fit a simple predictor of the fabrication rate on unseen subjects from properties of the injected data: the share of overlapping subjects, the number of distinct answers per relation and the frequency of each relation. Generate 60 fine-tuning mixtures of synthetic facts, fine-tune a 1B model on each, and measure the fabrication rate over 4 relation types. Test the predictor on 15 held-out mixtures with R-squared and rank correlation.
CONTROLS: A predictor using mixture size alone; a predictor with shuffled mixture properties; leave-one-out cross-validation; a fixed list of random seeds shared by all models.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: The predictor should explain over half of the variance on held-out mixtures, with overlap share the strongest term. It could fail if fabrication is dominated by training length.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Forecasting fabrication rates from the data mixture in language models
PROPOSAL: Fit a simple predictor of the fabrication rate on unseen subjects from properties of the injected data: the share of overlapping subjects, the number of distinct answers per relation and the frequency of each relation. Generate 200 fine-tuning mixtures of synthetic facts, fine-tune models of 160M, 410M and 1B parameters on each, and measure fabrication. Test the predictor on fifty held-out mixtures with R-squared and rank correlation, repeating each fit with 5 resamples.
CONTROLS: A predictor using mixture size alone; a predictor with shuffled mixture properties; leave-one-out cross-validation; paired bootstrap on the final scores.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: The predictor should explain most of the variance at all sizes. It could fail if the larger models change the relationship.
